If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (days 1–5) to counteract pessimism.  
When sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative (Δ > 0.5 in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast by 5–10% in late horizon (days 20–30) to hedge against reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending downward, add 3–7% downward bias in mid-horizon to align with momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending upward, add 3–7% upward bias in early horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >3% from true path, apply linear correction: subtract 0.5% per 2 days of sentiment volatility.
